title: Covalent bonding in water and carbon dioxide
caption: Each bond is a shared pair, one electron from each atom. Water has two O–H bonds and two lone pairs on oxygen; carbon dioxide has two C=O double bonds, each sharing two pairs. Every atom ends with a full outer shell.
alt: Dot-and-cross diagrams of water (two shared pairs and two lone pairs on oxygen) and carbon dioxide (two double bonds, two lone pairs on each oxygen).
description: Water: oxygen shares one pair with each hydrogen and keeps two lone pairs: eight around oxygen, two around each hydrogen.
Carbon dioxide: carbon shares two pairs with each oxygen; each oxygen keeps two lone pairs.
